stem:
Zubin lists $38$, $49$, and $70$ and wants to rule out impossible perfect squares using last-digit patterns. Perfect squares end only in $0$, $1$, $4$, $5$, $6$, or $9$.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims are correct?

options.text: $38$ cannot be a perfect square, because a perfect square cannot end in $8$.
$49$ cannot be ruled out by last digit alone, because $9$ is an allowed ending.
Reject $70$ only because the printed tens digit $7$ looks odd.

teacher.key_rationale: Last digit 8 forbids 38 as a square. Last digit 9 does not rule out 49. Labelling without the digit test, or rejecting 70 for its tens digit, miss the last-digit rule.
